fine_trace.note: When a session is removed (e.g. CloseSession), the session entry is removed from the list and a deferred cleanup callback is enqueued. The sentry (session_list_entry) remains alive in the delayed queue.

When cleanupCallback fires and calls UA_Session_deleteMembersCleanup, each subscription's delayedFreePointers is enqueued at HEAD of the same queue being processed, after the subscription's members are freed.

fine_trace.code: SIMPLEQ_FOREACH_SAFE(dc, &wq->delayedCallbacks, next, dc_tmp) { SIMPLEQ_REMOVE_HEAD(&wq->delayedCallbacks, next); if(dc->callback) dc->callback(dc->application, dc->data); UA_free(dc); }
fine_trace.note: SIMPLEQ_FOREACH_SAFE captures dc_tmp before the callback runs. Callbacks insert new items at HEAD via SIMPLEQ_INSERT_HEAD. SIMPLEQ_REMOVE_HEAD in the next iteration removes the newly-inserted HEAD (not the dc_tmp element), so items are freed in wrong order or missed. The session entry is freed (UA_free(dc) on cleanupCallback), leaving sub->session pointing to freed memory.

UA_free(dc) where dc == &sentry->cleanupCallback frees the session_list_entry (cleanupCallback is the first field). The subscription struct (sub) still has sub->session pointing into the freed sentry->session. In the second cleanup pass (UA_Server_delete -> UA_WorkQueue_cleanup), the leftover sub->delayedFreePointers or a second cleanup path dereferences the freed session memory.
